inScope: This record, committed first on the existing branch from baseCommit.

Saved place recovery on ChatGPT for a place far above the reader in a long conversation, from the cause observed on the site; the trust model (response-scoped anchors, no duplicate, safe unresolved outcome, stop on input, on a change of conversation and when Readela is off) is kept.

Saved place targeting without a selection: the first readable response paragraph that begins clearly below whatever covers the top of the reading area, found from the page's geometry. Return places the saved paragraph clearly below the same cover and reports success only then.
Inline code, keyboard and sample text under Paper and Night: a foreground, background and boundary of their own from theme tokens. Complete code blocks stay the site's.
A table with its wrappers as one coherent part of the reading surface, at its own width and with its sideways scrolling.
Popup: whether this conversation has a saved place and how many conversations have one; a refusal message at the capacity limit; a line naming the keyboard action.

Sidebar indicators: one data-readela attribute on the link of each conversation in the site's own lists that has a saved place, drawn as a small filled bookmark by the packaged stylesheet. The links' address paths are read in memory to derive the conversation key; no title, label or address is stored.
Capacity: 1000 saved conversations; a new conversation at the limit is refused and nothing is evicted; the stored format is unchanged.

Readela Sans: the official unmodified Inter variable fonts (roman and italic) packaged for Latin text beside Vazirmatn for Arabic script, each limited by unicode-range, with licence, version and digests recorded; two more web-accessible font files for the two supported hosts only. The visible choices stay Original and Readela Sans.

One keyboard action in the content script that saves or updates the place exactly as the popup's button does, ignored while typing; no new permission, no background script, no command registered with the browser.
Tests, fixtures, documentation and dated evidence made necessary by the above; a local unpacked Chrome build for owner review; an accurate description of pull request 9.

externalCapabilities.note: Load-bearing behaviour of the two supported sites, observed read-only in the owner's signed-in browser on 2026-10-10 before the contract was frozen: element names, attribute names, computed styles, geometry and counts only; no conversation text, title or address was recorded and nothing was typed or sent.

items.capability: ChatGPT: the conversation's scrolling region is a flex container with flex-direction column-reverse. Its scrollTop is 0 at the end of the conversation and negative above it; a positive value is clamped to 0.
items.authority: Observed: scrollTop set to 5000 read back as 0; set to -3000 read back as -3000; the minimum equalled minus the scrollable range.
items.probe: The ChatGPT fixture scrolls the same way; the end-to-end suite returns to a place far above from the end and to a place far below from the top.

items.capability: ChatGPT: a conversation opens with its last five turns in the document. Each time the beginning of the loaded part is scrolled into view, a batch of earlier turns is loaded and the scrollable range grows; only the turns near the viewport stay in the document, the others being replaced by an estimated height.
items.authority: Observed on one conversation: five turns and a range of about 5,200px at first; after the beginning was shown, a range of about 28,000px with six turns in the document; after the new beginning was shown, about 35,600px.
items.probe: A long ChatGPT fixture pages earlier turns in when its beginning is shown and keeps only nearby turns in the document.

items.capability: Claude: the transcript scrolls behind the chat header, which is positioned over the top of the scrolling region (48px, with an opaque band of 72px) and does not take pointer input, so a hit test passes through it. ChatGPT: the scrolling region begins below the fixed header and the composer overlays its lower edge.
items.authority: Observed geometry and computed position and pointer-events.
items.probe: The fixtures carry a cover over the top of the scrolling region that takes no pointer input (Claude) and a sticky bar inside it (ChatGPT).

items.capability: Sidebar rows: ChatGPT a[data-interactive-row-link] with href /c/<id> or /g/<project>/c/<id>; Claude a[data-row-main-button] with href /chat/<id>. Both are flex links whose ::after is unused and whose offset parent is the row.
items.probe: Fixtures with the same hooks, including rows added later and rows removed; where the hook is missing no row is marked.

items.capability: ChatGPT: a table sits in [data-markdown-table][data-wide-block] > a wrapper with overflow auto > a wrapper > table, with an absolutely positioned row of controls beside it. Claude: inline code is a code element with a border and background of its own inside reading text.
Neither site sets an accesskey attribute; the shortcuts the sites advertise in the page use Control (Control+K, Control+Shift+O).
items.authority: Observed in the documents of both sites; the browsers' own shortcut lists for Alt+Shift+S.
items.probe: The end-to-end suite presses the key in the page, in the composer and in an input.

items.capability: Inter is published by its author at github.com/rsms/inter under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, with variable web fonts in the release archive.
items.authority: The upstream release and its licence file, read when the asset is added; version, file names and digests recorded in src/fonts/README.md.
items.probe: The end-to-end suite asserts that Latin text is rendered with the packaged face, Arabic-script text with Vazirmatn, and that no request leaves the extension.

Inline code on ChatGPT in the conversations opened.
